claim:
For every real \(2<p<\infty\), let \(X_p\) be the Day--James plane on \(\mathbb R^2\) with
\[
\|(x,y)\|_{X_p}=
\begin{cases}
\bigl(|x|^p+|y|^p\bigr)^{1/p},&xy\ge0,\\
\max\{|x|,|y|\},&xy\le0.
\end{cases}
\]
Then its Ptolemy constant is exactly
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X_p)=1+2^{-2/p}.
\]
Since the published James constant of this family is \(J(X_p)=1+2^{-1/p}\), one has the exact identity
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X_p)=1+\bigl(J(X_p)-1\bigr)^2.
\]
integrity: The upper bound is a global Hilbert comparison proved on both sign sectors, and the lower bound is an exact explicit Ptolemy triple. No finite experiment or inaccessible source is used for correctness.
scientific_limitations: The theorem covers real two-dimensional Day--James ell_p-ell_infinity spaces with 2<p<infinity. It does not treat p<2, the infinite endpoint as part of the theorem, or general ell_p-ell_q planes. The 2015 reconsideration remains a bibliographic coverage risk because a readable full text was not obtained.
title: Exact Ptolemy constant of the Day--James \(\ell_p-\ell_\infty\) family above two
